title: When the Veil Sings Revisited
premise: Ansel Ravensworth, a temple scribe bound by debt to the silent gods of the Veil Valley, discovers that the old gods are answering prayers again — and that his own bloodline is the key they need. Hunted by the Inquisition and shadowed by a mercenary company who become his unlikely family, he must carry a fragment of divine song to the ruined heart of the old faith before the valley's magic-dead silence collapses entirely. In the end, Ansel chooses to shatter the secret rather than wield it, paying with his own voice to buy peace — and finding that a family of outlaws is worth more than any god's favor.
about_author: Ulyana Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval prayer books before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of the sacred.

chapters.title: The Silence That Pays
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet him copying prayers in a valley where magic cannot exist, chafing under his debt to the Temple of Quiet Hours. When a dying pilgrim's whispered plea is audibly answered by something ancient, Ansel realizes the silence has cracked. Emotional beat: restless longing curdling into fear.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Margins
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Investigating the answered prayer, Ansel finds his own handwriting appearing in old manuscripts — words he never wrote, in a language predating the valley. The Temple elders burn the evidence and warn him to forget it. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the first thrill of being chosen.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Inquisition arrives, claiming the valley's silence is failing and demanding the 'singer' responsible. Ansel's mentor sells him out to settle her own debts, and he flees across the valley's border — where magic floods back into the world and hits him like a tide. Emotional beat: betrayal and vertiginous freedom.

chapters.title: The Company of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, shifting to mercenary captain Sera Voss midway. Captured by a ragtag mercenary company of outcasts, Ansel bargains for his life by proving his scribe's value. Sera, skeptical but pragmatic, spares him. Emotional beat: wary transactional trust beginning to form.

chapters.title: What the Gods Owe
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The company takes a job escorting Ansel toward the ruined Heartspire, not knowing what he carries. Around campfires, Ansel learns their stories — each one a debt or injustice the law never fixed. He begins singing fragments involuntarily at night, and small miracles follow. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Inquisition burns a village that sheltered the company, and Ansel recognizes the lead inquisitor as his childhood friend Odile. She offers him amnesty if he surrenders the song. He refuses, and the company fights free at terrible cost — losing their youngest member. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; justice outside the law becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Song Beneath the Stone
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the Heartspire's threshold, Ansel confesses everything: the song can wake the old gods fully or seal them away forever, and either choice reignites the ancient war unless done at the exact place of binding. Sera must decide whether her company is escorts or executioners. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Torn between duty and memory, Odile reveals the Inquisition's true plan: not sealing the gods but caging them as weapons. She gives Ansel the final key — at the price of her own career and freedom. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming an ally through shared conscience.

chapters.title: Where the Veil Sings
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the Heartspire's heart, with the Inquisition closing in and the song pulling him apart, Ansel refuses both options offered — waking or caging. Instead he sings the binding backward, unmaking the secret inside himself, sacrificing his own voice to dissolve the gods' claim on the world. Emotional beat: climax; terrible cost accepted willingly.

chapters.title: Quiet Hours, Loud Hearts
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, closing with Ansel's. The valley's silence settles gently back, no longer a prison. Voiceless but free of debt, Ansel stays with the company as their chronicler, writing instead of singing. Odile sends word from exile: the world is learning new prayers. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; family chosen over divinity.
